title: ASCENT — The Cipher Worlds
subtitle: Adaptive Algebra I mastery, built to a Fortnite / Breath of the Wild bar
summary: The mastery question is answered, and the answer is the product's own thesis. The 0% that looked catastrophic was a starved measurement — the across-days arm was handed 1,275 items where the cram arm got 4,544, then printed beside it as though they were the same schooling. Measured properly, on the shipped route: cram 97.0%, which decays to 0.0% a week later. Daily 22-minute sittings 90.7%, still 89.0% a MONTH later. Every third day is 6.7%, and that one is real. Nobody bought those numbers by moving a dial — the frozen-competence table came out byte-identical.

pieces.name: World & art direction
pieces.note: Solid geometry has no down-facing light, so shadow renders pure black across up to 78% of a frame. A quarter of the places the game sends you are frames it refuses to compose.

pieces.name: Movement, camera & game feel
pieces.note: The on-screen jump, dash, glide and interact buttons never worked: a tap on the pad was eaten by the deafness that same tap created. Fixed and gated on nine phone profiles.

pieces.name: Axiom building system
pieces.note: Hand-built closed square; closing a room gives it a door.

pieces.name: Rift learning surface
pieces.note: The grader now demands the form the question asks for, and the keypad can finally type a bracket, a radical and an equals sign. check:answerable is green.

pieces.name: Content, item bank & mastery model
pieces.note: Level 2 went 78.5% to 91.5% true mastery, hollow claims 11.5% to 2.0%. Every dressed form had declared no scene keys, so the proving run could never be a transfer test.

pieces.name: EN / ES / PL localisation
pieces.note: 1072 keys x 3 locales, policed in src/ and content/.

pieces.name: Story, progression & session shape
pieces.note: Opening a new unit should be the biggest moment in the game. Right now it does not happen at all.

pieces.name: Post-processing & atmosphere
pieces.note: One golden hour, aerial perspective, volumetrics.

pieces.name: Audio & music
pieces.note: Synthesised adaptive score; the seal beat carries the payload.

pieces.name: Performance & platform reach
pieces.note: Fresh 120fps. Sustained-play measurement added after finding 44.9fps at minute 18.

pieces.name: Exact verification core
pieces.note: solveQuadratic with exact surd arithmetic, self-tested by planting wrong roots and unsimplified radicals and proving it rejects them.

pieces.name: Course progression
pieces.note: A cleared save returns the byte-identical shipped graph. Hold every line of Level 1 and a whole new region of the lattice opens, announced as a chapter plate rather than a level number.

pieces.name: Teacher record & standards
pieces.note: Both framework maps are derived from the running graph. Five units, both frameworks, every line carries its own standards and no unit prints another unit’s.

pieces.name: Invisible explicit teaching
pieces.note: Fifteen new counterexample handlers, enumerated from the packs rather than guessed. Every tagged slip in every unit is now answered with computed mathematics — it was 18% at Level 5.

pieces.name: The archipelago
pieces.note: Eight sites designed, five cut by the adversary. THE MEET is being built: the balance substitutes the cell under your boots live, so walking the rail is walking the solution set.

pieces.name: HUD, settings & phone frame
pieces.note: Build menu, sound and languages are off the glass. Strings on arrival went 76 to 8-11, and 119 to 9-10 in Polish. Two taps still land on the wrong control in landscape.

pieces.name: The 80% promise
pieces.note: Daily sittings hold at 90.7% and still 89.0% a month later. Cramming reaches 97% and keeps none of it. Every third day is 6.7% — real, and resting on two constants nobody has calibrated.

pieces.name: The reward loop
pieces.note: Seven minutes of sprinting with no questions answered pays 218 motes. A 22-minute session with 86 answers pays 74. The currency pays running ten times what it pays learning.

Client feedback from live play: collapse the build menu, move sound and languages to settings, three progress bars into one, and the jump button does nothing.

The jump button was never a regression — it had never worked. A touch fires pointerdown before touchstart, the handler read its own button as UI, and bought the world 0.16s of deafness that then swallowed the pad’s own press. It killed jump, dash, glide and interact.

A second bug found while hunting the first: the ORDERS card was capped without a scroller, so BEGIN THE RUN sat below the fold on a phone held sideways. That card holds uiOpen, which hides the touch pad — so every control in the game was dead on that device. 18 of 18 sizes and locales now reachable.
The across-days collapse was the instrument: sessions was hardcoded to 40, so the daily arm got 28% of the schooling and printed beside the cram arm under the words “the same 800 items”.
Measured properly: cramming reaches 97% and retains 0% a week later. Daily 22-minute sittings reach 90.7% and retain 89.0% a month later. That is the whole thesis of the product, in one table.
The gate built to catch the answer-shape leak was averaging 26,436 real choice cards with 63,558 cards whose options a learner never sees, and printing PASS.

A critic suspects three rounds of “the sitting is a worksheet” may be partly an artefact: the RUN CLOSED card takes the whole frame and Escape does not dismiss it, and the motion gate’s own sitting was spent behind one.
